claims.text: A Hays County Commissioners Court agenda published at seq=135 is headed for a meeting on September 1st, 2026.
claims.note: The separator rendered by the page is an en dash, preserved because a verbatim quote is never touched.
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 1st, 2026

claims.text: That September 1st agenda carried an item acknowledging that the Hays County Sheriff's Office had committed not to activate or implement Axon Draft One.
claims.quote: Acknowledgement of the Hays County Sheriff's Office's commitment to not activate or implement Axon Draft One
claims.note: Item 18 under the section headed CONSENT ITEMS, not item 18 of the agenda as a whole.
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 1st, 2026

claims.text: The agenda item itself describes Axon Draft One as a report-writing feature inside the Axon AI Era platform.
claims.quote: an AI-enabled report-writing feature within the Axon AI Era platform
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 1st, 2026

claims.text: The same item extends the commitment to any new AI-based features the platform may later make available, and conditions their operational use on the Commissioners Court granting approval first.
claims.quote: any new AI-based features the Axon AI Era platform may make available under the related contract without returning to the Hays County Commissioners Court for approval
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 1st, 2026

claims.text: The Axon Draft One item names Becerra and Hipolito on its sponsor line.
claims.quote: Hays County Commissioners Court for approval. BECERRA/HIPOLITO
claims.note: Sponsor names render in bold immediately after the item's closing full stop.
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 1st, 2026

claims.text: A second Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, at seq=136, is headed for a meeting on September 15th, 2026.
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 15th, 2026

claims.text: The September 15th agenda carried an item to authorize the County Clerk's Office to obtain AI Minutes from Govably, Inc.
claims.quote: authorize the County Clerk's Office to obtain AI Minutes through Govably, Inc.
claims.note: Item 6 under the section headed MISCELLANEOUS, not item 6 of the agenda as a whole.
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 15th, 2026

claims.text: The Govably item states the first year's amount as $19,200.00.
claims.quote: in the amount of $19,200.00 for year one
claims.note: Transcribed exactly as printed. Nothing was converted, summed or rounded.
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 15th, 2026

claims.text: The same item asks the Court to waive the county purchasing policy that requires three quotes.
claims.quote: authorize a waiver to the purchasing policy of obtaining three quotes
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 15th, 2026

claims.text: The Govably item names Becerra, Cardenas and Hunt on its sponsor line.
claims.quote: purchasing policy of obtaining three quotes. BECERRA/CARDENAS/HUNT
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 15th, 2026

claims.text: A third Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, at seq=141, is headed for a meeting on September 8th, 2026.
claims.note: This header sets the month in mixed case where the other two set it in capitals. Reproduced as found.
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 8th, 2026

claims.text: The September 8th agenda carried an item on the use, implementation, oversight and governance of artificial intelligence in connection with surveillance equipment and related services.
claims.quote: regarding the use, implementation, oversight, and governance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in connection with surveillance equipment, technologies, programs, software, systems, data collection, data analysis, and related services
claims.note: Item 2 under the section headed MISCELLANEOUS.
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 8th, 2026

claims.text: That item contemplated adopting a policy statement setting guidelines, standards, safeguards and limits on AI-enabled surveillance technologies used by the county.
claims.quote: possible adoption of a policy statement establishing guidelines, standards, safeguards, and limitations concerning the use of AI-enabled surveillance technologies by Hays County
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 8th, 2026

claims.text: The item listed immediately after the AI surveillance item on the September 8th agenda concerns two contract amendments with Tyler Technologies, one of them for report writing services.
claims.quote: one for NG911 interface and one for report writing services
claims.note: Item 3 under MISCELLANEOUS, directly after item 2. No relationship to the Axon item is asserted or evidenced.
claims.document: Hays County Commissioners Court agenda, September 8th, 2026

claims.text: The county's own Court Minutes 2026 archive lists no meeting later than July 28th, 2026, so no minutes for any September 2026 meeting appear there.
claims.note: Entries are listed newest first and the quote is the top of that list as the page renders it. Two independent reads found no entry for August or September 2026.
claims.document: Hays County Archive Center, Court Minutes 2026

claims.text: Axon's own product page says Draft One uses generative AI and body-worn camera audio to produce draft report narratives.
claims.quote: leveraging generative AI and body-worn camera audio to produce high-quality draft report narratives in seconds
claims.note: A vendor's description of its own product, not a finding by any public body.

claims.text: Axon's product page also states that a Draft One narrative can't be submitted without an officer reviewing and approving it.
claims.quote: these narratives cannot be submitted without officer review and approval
claims.note: Vendor claim about its own product.

claims.text: Govably's own site says its product uses AI to write official meeting minutes from a recording, a live session or a pasted transcript.
claims.quote: Govably uses AI to write official meeting minutes from any source

rejected.finding: The Court Minutes 2026 archive has an exact list length of 14 entries.
rejected.reason: No numeral stating a count appears on the page. The figure was produced by a model reading a rendered list and no verbatim quote proves it. The newest posted date is recorded instead, as c15.

rejected.finding: Item 18 on the September 1st agenda, item 6 on the September 15th agenda, item 2 and item 3 on the September 8th agenda.
rejected.reason: Corrected rather than dropped. These are section-relative numbers. Agenda item 6 of the September 15th meeting as a whole is a different item reading Approve Utility Permit.

rejected.finding: The full text of the Tyler Technologies item, including a colon after the company name.
rejected.reason: Two reads disagreed on the disputed character, so the quote in c14 was cut back to the span both reads returned identically.

rejected.finding: That any of the three AI items passed, failed, was tabled, amended or withdrawn.
rejected.reason: No outcome is published on any of the three agenda pages, and the minutes archive carries nothing later than July 28th, 2026. An agenda states what was scheduled and never what was decided.

rejected.finding: That the Court gave opposite answers on whether a machine may write an official record.
rejected.reason: Unsupported by any source. What is evidenced is that two items with opposing postures toward AI-written records appeared on agendas two weeks apart. Whether either was adopted is unpublished, so no comparison of outcomes can be made.

rejected.finding: A relationship between the Tyler Technologies report writing services amendment and the Axon Draft One item.
rejected.reason: Not asserted and not evidenced. They appear on different agendas and nothing on either page connects them. c14 records adjacency only.
